FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 3 July 1989, after the 
draft finalized by the Small Tools Sectional Committee, had been approved by the Mechanical 
Engineering Division Council. 

These carbide tips are designated as *HD' as decided by the Committee to distinguish from other 
carbide tips and are intended for use on dead centres after suitably fixing and grinding to the 
dimensions according to IS 2534 : 1963 'Carbide tipped dead centres. 

In the preparation of this standard assistance has been derived from the practices prevalent in 
Indian industries. 



AMENDMENT NO. 1 SEPTEMBER 2000 

TO

CENTRES — SPECIFICATION 

( Page \, clause 4 ) — Insert the following at the end of the clause: 
'Unless otherwise specified the carbide tip shall be of K 10 grade.'

Indian Standard 



CARBIDE TIPS FOR DEAD CENTRES 
SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

This standard covers the dimensions and other 
requirements for carbide tips for dead centre 
covered in IS 2534 : 1963 'Carbide tipped dead 
centres'. 

2 REFERENCE 

18 7778:1975 Methods for sampling small 
tools. 

3 DIMENSIONS 

Dimensions of carbide tips for dead centres 
shall be as given in Table 1 . 

4 MATERIAL 

Material of carbide tips shall be of a suitable 
wear resistance grade as agreed to by the 
manufacturer and the user. 

5 GENERAL REQ]UIREMENTS 

Carbide tips shall be free from cracks and any 
visual defects. 



6 SAMPLING 

The sampling and criteria of acceptance shall 
be according to IS 7778 : 1975. 

7 DESIGNATION 

A carbide tip of type HD5 conforming to 
this standard shall be designated as: 

Carbide tip HD5 IS 12728 

8 MARKING 

Each carton containing carbide tips shall be 
marked with quantity, designation and manu- 
facturers name and/or trade-mark. 

9 PACKING AND PACKAGING 

The carbide tips shall be suitably packed to 
avoid damage in handling. 



IS 12728 : 1989

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards 
Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products 
covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with 
the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality 
control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked 
products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safe- 
guard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted 
to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bnreaii of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Actf 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification 
of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in 
the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or 
grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), 
BIS. 

Revision of Indian Standards 

Indian Standards are reviewed periodically and revised, when necessary and amendments, if any, 
are issued from time to time. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in 
possession of the latest amendments or edition. Comments on this Indian Standard may be sent 
to BIS giving the following reference: 

Doc : No. EDC 45/PED 12 ( 4815 )
